ReleaseLabel: ai_router [Unreleased] -- Set 109 'Model Registry and Pricing Truth', Session 4 of 4: the price-confirmation walk
Notes:
This set exists because router-config.yaml recorded $2.50/$15.00 for a model that bills $5.00/$30.00, and nothing said so for four months and $51 of unreported spend. The fix is not a better scraper -- it is that a HUMAN now confirms every rate before it is written.

So the thing under test is the confirmation screen. If you cannot read a proposed price change and decide about it, the whole design fails open and we get another silent placeholder with better manners. Four items, because that criterion has four halves: can you READ it, does REJECT really not write, does ACCEPT really write, and can you be tricked into writing something you did not read.

EVERYTHING BELOW RUNS ON A THROWAWAY COPY. Step 1 copies router-config.yaml to your temp folder and every later command points at the copy with --config. The real registry is never touched, so you can get any of this wrong with no consequence. That is deliberate: a walk you are afraid of is a walk that gets rushed.

You need: a terminal in the repo root, the venv, and about ten minutes. The commands are literal -- copy and paste them.

QUALITY BAR, said once so it is not repeated per item: judge these screens as if you had never seen this codebase. If a line made you re-read it, guess, or go looking for something that was not there, that is a defect and it goes in Feedback -- even if you worked out the right answer in the end. Working it out is exactly what the operator on a Friday afternoon will not do.

Passes: false means NOT YET WALKED, not "failed".

Review.Subarea: A proposed price change is legible to a human
Review.ItemLabel: You can say what each proposed change means, and spot the planted wrong rate, without help
Review.HumanAction:
Where you are: a terminal at the repo root. Nothing has been run yet.

1. Make the throwaway copy and plant one obviously wrong rate in it:

     copy ai_router\router-config.yaml %TEMP%\uat-config.yaml

   Open %TEMP%\uat-config.yaml in an editor, find the block that starts with
     gpt-5-4:
   and change its input_cost_per_1m from 2.50 to 99.00. Save.

2. Ask the tool what the providers publish today:

     .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m ai_router.pricing_proposal --fetch --config %TEMP%\uat-config.yaml --proposal %TEMP%\uat-proposal.json

3. Read the output on screen. Do not open the JSON yet.
Review.Expectation:
The run ends with this line:
  3 rate change(s) and 0 confirmation(s) to review. Nothing has been written. Set each "decision" to "accept" or "reject" in the proposal file, then run --apply.

One of the three is the rate you planted, and it reads:
  [~] gpt-5-4 (openai / gpt-5.4) -- https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing
      currently recorded:
        in $99.0 / out $15.0 per 1M
      the page says:
        in $2.5 / out $15.0 per 1M

Without looking anything up, you should be able to answer: which number is yours, which is OpenAI's, and which way the change goes.

Review.Subarea: A change you refuse is not written
Review.ItemLabel: Rejecting every change leaves the config byte-for-byte alone
Review.HumanAction:
Where you are: %TEMP%\uat-proposal.json exists and every change in it says "decision": "pending".

1. Open %TEMP%\uat-proposal.json in an editor.
2. Find all three occurrences of
     "decision": "pending"
   and change each to
     "decision": "reject"
   Save.
3. Apply:

     .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m ai_router.pricing_proposal --apply --config %TEMP%\uat-config.yaml --proposal %TEMP%\uat-proposal.json

4. Check the planted rate is still wrong -- that is the point:

     findstr "99.00" %TEMP%\uat-config.yaml
Review.Expectation:
Step 3 prints exactly:
  [ ] Nothing accepted; router-config.yaml is unchanged.

Step 4 still finds the planted line:
      input_cost_per_1m: 99.00

The tool knew the right answer, said so on screen, and did not write it. That refusal is the entire safety property.
Review.ProgrammaticVerification: ai_router/tests/test_pricing_proposal.py::test_apply_with_nothing_accepted_leaves_the_config_alone and ::test_fetch_never_writes_the_config. Walked by the orchestrator on 2026-08-04 with the output quoted above.

Review.Subarea: A change you approve is written, and dated
Review.ItemLabel: Accepting one change writes that rate and stamps it, and leaves the other two alone
Review.HumanAction:
Where you are: everything is still marked reject and nothing has been written.

1. Open %TEMP%\uat-proposal.json again. Find the change whose "alias" is
     gpt-5-4
   and change ONLY that one back to
     "decision": "accept"
   Leave the other two on "reject". Save.
2. Apply:

     .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m ai_router.pricing_proposal --apply --config %TEMP%\uat-config.yaml --proposal %TEMP%\uat-proposal.json

3. Look at what it wrote:

     findstr /C:"input_cost_per_1m: 2.5" /C:"confirmed_on" /C:"99.00" %TEMP%\uat-config.yaml
Review.Expectation:
Step 2 prints exactly two lines:
  [x] wrote gpt-5-4 and stamped confirmed_on
  Updated %TEMP%\uat-config.yaml

Step 3 shows the corrected rate and a stamp carrying today's date:
      input_cost_per_1m: 2.5
      confirmed_on: '2026-08-04'

and finds NO remaining 99.00 -- the planted rate is gone.

The two you left on reject were not written: the tool reported one alias, not three.

Review.Subarea: You cannot apply a proposal you did not finish reading
Review.ItemLabel: One undecided change refuses the whole apply, naming what is undecided
Review.HumanAction:
Where you are: the previous item wrote one rate. This one checks the guard that stops a skim.

1. Start over with a fresh proposal:

     .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m ai_router.pricing_proposal --fetch --config %TEMP%\uat-config.yaml --proposal %TEMP%\uat-proposal.json

2. Open %TEMP%\uat-proposal.json. Mark ONE change "accept" and leave the rest on "pending" -- exactly what someone does when they read the first entry and get interrupted.
3. Try to apply:

     .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m ai_router.pricing_proposal --apply --config %TEMP%\uat-config.yaml --proposal %TEMP%\uat-proposal.json

4. When you are done, delete the throwaway files:

     del %TEMP%\uat-config.yaml %TEMP%\uat-proposal.json
Review.Expectation:
Step 3 refuses, names every undecided entry, and writes nothing:
  [x] REFUSED: 2 change(s) are still 'pending': claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5. Every change must be marked 'accept' or 'reject' before any of them is written.

The one you marked "accept" was NOT written either. That is the intended behaviour: applying the parts someone read and skipping the parts they did not is how a machine ends up writing a price no human weighed.

(The two names may differ if the registry has changed since 2026-08-04. What must hold is that it refuses, names them, and writes nothing.)
